business_problem: BBC Archives Technology and Services needed to preserve and unify a 100-year archive of media assets, reduce the cost and physical footprint of tape-based infrastructure, and improve access to content while preparing the archive for future machine-learning use cases.
solution_summary: BBC Archives Technology and Services migrated its flagship archive to AWS to preserve 100 years of content and modernize access to 16 million media assets. Using AWS Direct Connect, the team transferred archive data over the network at scale into Amazon S3 storage, with the bulk of content placed in Amazon S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval for low-cost access and additional optimization through Amazon S3 Intelligent-Tiering. The cloud design replaced tape-based repositories with a next-generation abstraction between media asset management systems and public cloud storage, allowing the BBC to keep archive content durable, accessible, and better prepared for future machine-learning use cases. Centralizing the archive on S3 also improves data availability, simplifies access for archive teams, and lets the BBC retire a significant amount of physical infrastructure while reducing overall storage cost.

solution_components.name: AWS Direct Connect
solution_components.role: Transfers large archive datasets from BBC infrastructure into AWS over dedicated network connections.

solution_components.name: Amazon S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval
solution_components.role: Stores the bulk of archive media in a low-cost class that still supports expedited retrieval.

solution_components.name: Amazon S3 Intelligent-Tiering
solution_components.role: Optimizes storage placement for archive content with changing access patterns.

data_flow: Archive content is transferred over AWS Direct Connect into Amazon S3-based storage, with most media held in Amazon S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval and additional optimization through Amazon S3 Intelligent-Tiering before the content is exposed back to archive and media-management workflows.
business_outcome: The BBC migrated 25 PB of data in 10 months at peak rates of 120 TB per day, retired half of its archive physical infrastructure, improved content accessibility, and reduced overall infrastructure costs while preserving 100 years of archive material.
